article.title: CEO of Mistral: AI is software. It can be controlled

editorial:
The Robot Has an Off Switch. Does Anyone Know Where? 🤖

Arthur Mensch, CEO of France’s Mistral AI, offers a refreshingly practical thought: AI is software, and software can be controlled. That sounds obvious until a chatbot confidently invents an answer. The question isn’t whether people can influence these systems. It’s whether we design controls that ordinary people can actually understand and use. 🎛️

A great product makes complexity disappear without hiding responsibility. For AI, that means clear limits, visible sources where possible, meaningful human oversight and a way to correct mistakes. An off switch is useful; knowing when to reach for it is better. Trust should come from what a system does, not how fluently it speaks.

Mistral’s place in the European AI race makes this more than a design question. Whoever builds the tools helps set expectations for everyone else. The opportunity is to make powerful software feel less like magic and more like something we can examine, challenge and improve. That would be a breakthrough worth getting excited about. ✨

by Steve Jobs
